metadata.description: Curated dataset of open source ERP/CRM projects for Clean Architecture evaluation

projects.name: Odoo
projects.description: Comprehensive open-source ERP and CRM suite. Monolithic framework with a proprietary ORM, web framework, and business logic tightly integrated into modules.
notable_characteristics: Custom ORM where business logic is embedded in model methods
No clear separation between domain logic and persistence
Controllers tightly coupled to Odoo's HTTP framework
Module system provides some separation at macro level
Heavy use of inheritance and monkey-patching

projects.name: ERPNext
projects.description: Cloud ERP system built on top of the Frappe framework. Business logic is organized in DocType-based modules tightly coupled to the Frappe ORM and metadata system.
notable_characteristics: DocType system tightly couples metadata, validation and persistence
Business logic spread across controller.py and model hooks
No explicit use case or application service layer
Frappe framework deeply embedded in all layers
Some domain logic in utility modules but not consistently separated

projects.name: Tryton
projects.description: Modular three-tier high-level general purpose application platform, used as ERP. Features clear module boundaries and a protocol-based client-server separation.
notable_characteristics: Clear separation between server core (trytond) and modules
Protocol-based communication between client and server layers
Model layer uses descriptors but still tied to the Tryton ORM
Wizard pattern provides a basic application service layer
Consistent use of IR (Information Repository) for metadata

projects.name: SuiteCRM
projects.description: Enterprise-grade open source CRM forked from SugarCRM. Legacy architecture with intertwined database queries, business logic and presentation in many places.
notable_characteristics: Active Record pattern: domain objects directly extend SugarBean (database entity)
SQL queries embedded in business logic and view files
Limited use of interfaces or abstractions for external dependencies
Module structure provides macro-level separation
Some refactoring towards services in recent versions but inconsistent

projects.name: EspoCRM
projects.description: Modern CRM with a clean PHP architecture. Uses dependency injection, service layers, and repository patterns, showing better separation than older PHP CRMs.
notable_characteristics: Separate Entity, Repository and Service layers
Dependency injection container used throughout the application
Entities are relatively thin data objects with some domain logic
Services handle business logic but have some infrastructure coupling
Repository pattern abstracts data access

projects.name: Dolibarr
projects.description: Web-based ERP and CRM for small and medium businesses. Predominantly procedural PHP with class-based models that include direct database calls, minimal layering.
notable_characteristics: Classes directly execute SQL queries (Active Record with manual SQL)
Business logic, HTML, and database access mixed in page scripts
No service layer or use case abstraction
Global functions in lib/ directories used across all modules
Very little use of interfaces or dependency injection

projects.name: OroCRM
projects.description: Enterprise CRM built on Oro Platform and Symfony. Uses Symfony best practices: Doctrine repositories, service layer, event-driven architecture and clear bundle separation.
notable_characteristics: Symfony bundle structure provides clear module boundaries
Doctrine repositories cleanly separate persistence from domain
Service layer using Symfony DI with interface-based abstractions
Event-driven communication between bundles reduces coupling
Some domain logic still leaks into Symfony controllers

projects.name: metasfresh
projects.description: Cloud-ready ERP built with Java and Spring Boot. Organized into bounded contexts with clear separation of API, model, and repository layers. Uses DDD tactical patterns.
notable_characteristics: Bounded contexts map to Maven modules with explicit boundaries
Interfaces (Java API) define contracts between layers
Repository pattern with Spring Data abstracts persistence
Domain services separate from infrastructure services
Some legacy ADempiere code still uses active record pattern

projects.name: iDempiere
projects.description: OSGi-based ERP using the ADempiere data model. Plugin architecture provides strong module isolation, but domain objects extend from a generated base layer tied to the database schema.
notable_characteristics: Generated model classes (MTable, MOrder, etc.) extend PO (Persistent Object)
OSGi plugins allow strong module boundary enforcement
Process classes provide a form of use-case separation
Domain models directly access the database via the PO base class
Interface-based plugin API for cross-plugin communication

projects.name: Vtiger CRM
projects.description: Open source CRM evolved from SugarCRM. Retains legacy Active Record patterns but adds a handler and event system. Business logic, persistence, and presentation remain somewhat mixed.
notable_characteristics: Modules extend CRMEntity (Active Record base class with database access)
Handler system adds some event-driven separation
Vtlib provides utility abstractions but coupling remains high
Limited use of dependency injection or inversion of control
Some newer code shows cleaner patterns but inconsistently applied
